references.text: Psalm 136:7-9 mentions God's creation of the great lights, the sun to rule over the day and the moon and stars to rule over the night, as part of God's enduring love and power.
Psalm 8:3 describes how humanity looks at the sky, the moon, and the stars, which God's fingers have formed, and reflects on humanity's place in creation.
Deuteronomy 4:19 warns Israel against worshipping the sun, the moon, and the stars, which God has assigned to all nations under the whole heaven.
Psalm 104:19 states that God set the moon to mark the seasons and that the sun knows when to set, reflecting God's ordering of the heavenly bodies in Gen 1:16.
Jeremiah 31:35 refers to the Lord who gives the sun for light by day and sets fixed orders for the moon and stars to give light by night, a direct parallel to Gen 1:16.
Isaiah 40:26 urges one to lift up their eyes to the heavens and see who has created the stars, bringing them out as an army—relevant to the mention of the stars in Gen 1:16.
Hebrews 11:3 speaks of how by faith we understand that the universe was formed at God's command, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible.
Contrast between the created order (sun/moon governing day/night) and God's direct guidance (cloud pillar/fire pillar) which breaks this order to show the way.
The creation account of the heavenly bodies (Gen 1:16) is theologically interpreted in the psalm as testifying to God's glory (Ps 19:2).
